title: The mate comparison in a square of adjunctions
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-conjugate-pull-iso] (only the adjunctions
$E_1\dashv\mathrm{Res}_1$ and $E_2\dashv\mathrm{Res}_2$ are needed), the *mate* of
$e^{-1}\colon L_1\circ\mathrm{Res}_1\to\mathrm{Res}_2\circ L_2$ is the natural transformation

$$
E_2\circ L_1\longrightarrow L_2\circ E_1\colon\mathcal A\longrightarrow\mathcal B',
$$

the composite
$E_2L_1\xrightarrow{E_2L_1\eta_1}E_2L_1\mathrm{Res}_1E_1\xrightarrow{E_2e^{-1}E_1}
E_2\mathrm{Res}_2L_2E_1\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_2L_2E_1}L_2E_1$, with $\eta_1$ the unit of
$E_1\dashv\mathrm{Res}_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$ the counit of $E_2\dashv\mathrm{Res}_2$. It is not
an isomorphism in general.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: TwoSquare.natTrans ((CategoryTheory.mateEquiv adj₁ adj₂).symm (TwoSquare.mk Res₁ L₂ L₁ Res₂ e.inv)), where adj₁ : E₁ ⊣ Res₁ and adj₂ : E₂ ⊣ Res₂. Set the Mathlib categories C,D,E,F to A,B,A′,B′, its horizontal left adjoints L₁,L₂ to E₁,E₂, and its vertical functors G,H to the item’s L₁,L₂. The inverse construction in Mates.lean:93-100 is exactly the displayed unit–e.inv–counit composite, with functor associators and unitors; TwoSquare and its mk/natTrans are just natural transformations (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Functor/TwoSquare.lean:50,55,59). The remark about failure of invertibility is a caveat, not an added IsIso hypothesis; Mates.lean:81 explicitly makes the same caveat. The free-monoid counit example in report.md verifies it even when the vertical functors also have left adjoints. No use of the conjugate isomorphism or of the vertical adjunctions is required.
